source.section: Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 135,750.00 = 135,750.00. Federal taxable income = 135,750.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 120,000.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing separately. Line 9 federal AGI 135,750.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 135,750.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 27,500.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15 PIT-ADJ deductions and exemptions 0.00. Line 17 = 135,750.00 + 0.00 - 15,750.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 120,000.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 120,000.00 = 120,000.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 120,000.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 4,000.00 = 60 + 3.2% x 8,500.00 = 272 + 4.3% x 12,500.00 = 537.5 + 4.7% x 25,000.00 = 1,175 + 4.9% x 70,000.00 = 3,430; total 5,474.5, to the cent 5,474.50. The printed section on T-7 gives 5,472.00; expected keeps the schedule figure 5,474.50, 2.50 more. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 5,474.50.
accepted_approximations: Over 100,000 the printed section is base plus rate, and each base is the table's last row (midpoint 99,950), not the tax at 100,000. A bracket schedule cannot hold that step down, so the schedule gives more than the printed section at every income over 100,000.
